title: 1971 AHSME Problem 30
statement: Given the linear fractional transformation \[ f_1(x)=\frac{2x-1}{x+1}, \] define \(f_{n+1}(x)=f_1(f_n(x))\) for \(n=1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(\ldots.\) Assuming \(f_{35}(x)=f_5(x),\) it follows that \(f_{28}(x)\) is equal to:

solutions.text:
The transformation is invertible. From \(f_{35}=f_5,\) composing with \(f_5^{-1}\) shows that \(f_{30}\) is the identity. Solving \(y=\frac{2x-1}{x+1}\) for \(x\) gives \[ g(y)=f_1^{-1}(y)=\frac{y+1}{2-y}. \] Since iterates have period \(30,\) \(f_{28}=f_{-2}=g^2.\) Direct composition gives \[ g(g(x))=\frac{1}{1-x}. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Cancel five iterates by composing with the inverse transformation
If \(g=f_1^{-1}\), then \(f_{28}=g^2\) once \(f_{30}\) is the identity
